objective: Test whether exact Bayesian observation history creates a reward incentive beyond the best constant-action policy.

rejected_cycle_5_effect_size_variant_2.certificate_interpretation: When true, this feasible belief policy's lower approximate confidence limit exceeds the exact best constant return, so no constant policy can be Bayes optimal for this finite horizon.
rejected_cycle_5_effect_size_variant_2.filter: source <- normalize(source @ pending_edge[token]); belief <- source @ transition[pending_action]
rejected_cycle_5_effect_size_variant_2.policy: condition the exact six-state belief on delayed tokens and executed actions, then maximize expected next-step occupancy
rejected_cycle_5_effect_size_variant_2.reward_timing: reward is pre-transition occupancy, so the current action is ranked by its effect on the next decision's expected reward
rejected_cycle_5_effect_size_variant_2.status: Monte Carlo value of a feasible exact-filter policy, not the Bayes-optimal POMDP value
